newsitem.title: USA: Jackson hails setback to Calif. ban on preferences.
newsitem.headline: Jackson hails setback to Calif. ban on preferences.

text.p: Civil rights activist Jesse Jackson Thursday welcomed a court ruling that temporarily blocked enforcement of a controversial measure to roll back affirmative action programs in California.

"States do not have the right to curtail any American civil rights," he said in a written statement. "We're glad the judge will give supporters of equal rights and diversity a chance to make their case."

U.S. District Judge Thelton Henderson of San Francisco agreed to a request Wednesday by civil rights groups to issue a temporary restraining order barring Gov. Pete Wilson and California Attorney General Dan Lungren from implementing the measure, called Proposition 209.

His decision bars enforcement of the initiative which would prohibit racial or gender preferences in public employment, education or contracting in California. Californians voted 54-46 percent Nov. 5 to make Proposition 209 part of the state constitution.

The judge's order remains in effect until Dec. 16, when he will hear the civil rights groups' arguments for a preliminary injunction that would freeze Proposition 209 until a trial can be held on the measure's constitutionality.
The initiative, the first of its kind passed by any state, would eliminate most California affirmative action programs designed to broaden opportunities for women and racial minorities.
A day after the election, civil rights groups sued to block Proposition 209 on behalf of labor, education, women's business groups and minority organizations, arguing it was unconstitutional.
